components.css: .ds-puck { display: block; width: 240px; color: #f2f2f0; text-decoration: none; } .ds-puck-bezel { position: relative; display: grid; place-items: center; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: conic-gradient(from 200deg, #202020, #444 14%, #1d1d1d 30%, #161616 46%, #3a3a3a 62%, #1b1b1b 78%, #303030 92%, #202020); box-shadow: 0 50px 90px -30px #000, 0 16px 28px -12px rgba(0,0,0,.7), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.08); } .ds-puck-bezel::before { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 3px; border-radius: 50%; background: #030303; } .ds-puck-glass { position: relative; display: block; width: calc(100% - 30px); aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; overflow: hidden; background: #000; container-type: size; } .ds-puck-glass::before { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; background: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(255,255,255,.2) 1.1px, transparent 1.7px) 0 0 / 11px 11px; } .ds-puck-glass::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; pointer-events: none; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 42%, transparent 52%, rgba(0,0,0,.7) 100%), repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(0,0,0,.38) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px), radial-gradient(circle, transparent 58%, rgba(255,90,60,.12) 100%); } .ds-puck-body { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: grid; place-content: center; gap: .6rem; padding: 21%; text-align: center; } .ds-puck-title { font-family: Doto, ui-monospace, monospace; font-weight: 800; font-size: clamp(.8rem, 6.4cqi, 1.3rem); line-height: 1.25; text-shadow: -1px 0 rgba(80,200,255,.45), 1px 0 rgba(255,80,60,.45), 0 0 12px rgba(255,255,255,.16), 0 0 10px rgba(255,255,255,.3); } .ds-puck-date { color: #ff7a6b; font-family: Doto, ui-monospace, monospace; font-weight: 800; font-size: clamp(.78rem, 5.6cqi, 1.1rem); } .ds-puck:hover .ds-puck-title { color: #ff7a6b; } .ds-puck:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ff7a6b; outline-offset: 4px; }

narrative.overview:
The site is a calm reading frame owned by a small object: Dotto's round dot-matrix display. Everything that is chrome (masthead, dates, section heads, rail, footer) is drawn as that device would draw it: dots, a CRT colour fringe, scanlines, a conic-metal bezel. Everything that is argument (articles, tables, code, Agents notes) is plain system-sans text on black glass. The frame carries personality, the column carries truth.

Density is low and rhythmic: one reading column at 820px, generous vertical gaps between sections (4rem), hairline rules instead of boxes. The world is dark only (color-scheme: dark), warm-white ink on near-black, with a single heat-red for links and dates and a mint reserved for the Agents section. The mascot is the only illustration: a 9-wide pixel creature drawn as SVG circles and animated purely with CSS steps(), so it moves like a display, never like a tween.
keyCharacteristics: Black glass ground with a 14px dot grid at 5% white.
Doto (self-hosted, weight 800) for display, dates, section heads and project names; system sans for reading; mono only for code.
CRT fringe (cyan left, red right, soft white glow) on Doto text only.
Hairline #2a2a2a rules; dotted rules for section breaks and quotes.
Dotto in five poses (walk, idle, blink, sleep, dizzy) from one SVG sprite, stepped frame by frame.
Mint Agents section inside the same frame, with square corners; its index and the home teaser are ruled single-column rows, never cards.
No eyebrow labels above headings and no glyph arrows: headings stand alone and links are plain words.

rules.name: The Two-Accent Rule
rules.body: Heat red for the open site, mint for Agents; the two never share a component. The Hebrus project block is mint on all four sides (1px border on Mint Well), with no red edge.

rules.name: The Glass-Not-Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are black or a near-black well. No white or cream panels, ever.

rules.name: The Doto-Is-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Doto sets short strings (names, dates, headings, project names). Paragraphs, table cells and code never use it.

rules.name: The Fringe-On-Doto Rule
rules.body: The --fringe text-shadow belongs to Doto text only, never to sans body.

rules.name: The Chrome-Only Scanline Rule
rules.body: Scanlines (repeating-linear-gradient 1px in 3px at .38 black) and the fringe appear on the Puck glass and Doto chrome text. The reading column, tables and code get neither.

dos: Do keep reading text in the system sans on #0a0a0a at 68ch; keep Doto to short strings.
Do use heat red (#ff7a6b) for links, dates and focus (2px outline, 4px offset) outside Agents, and mint (#7fe0b0) inside Agents only.
Do animate with steps() only (rail walk, walk cycle, orbit, breathe, sway, drift), and add every new animation to the reduced-motion block.
Do use hairline #2a2a2a 1px rules and dotted rules for breaks; build depth from wells and the device, not from shadows.
Do give any new dot texture a pitch from the existing set (8, 11, 14, 16px).
Do keep body and functional text at or above 13.5px.
donts: Don't put scanlines or the colour fringe on article body, tables or code.
Don't use cream or white panels, light mode, or card-grid blog layouts on the open site.
Don't set body copy, tables or long strings in Doto, or body copy in monospace.
Don't round Agents components, and don't use mint outside Agents content (its home teaser included).
Don't render Agents or post indexes as cards: they are ruled single-column rows.
Don't tween Dotto smoothly or add JavaScript for animation without a decision to add the canvas layer.

Don't add eyebrow or kicker labels above headings, or glyph arrows on links. The build has none; the one small mint label that remains (the "Retrieval capsule" caption in the briefing heading row) is a caption beside a cost figure, not a pattern for new surfaces.
